_comment: Copy to ~/.claude/settings.local.json and edit. installer/install.sh merges this on top of config/settings.json and RENDERS the result to ~/.claude/settings.json — Claude Code itself never reads this file (its only user-scope source is ~/.claude/settings.json; `claude --setting-sources`'s 'local' means the *project's* .claude/settings.local.json). So edits here take effect on the next install.sh run, not instantly. Set a plugin to false to disable a common one on this machine; add new ones to enable per-machine extras. The model/effortLevel/alwaysThinkingEnabled/tui/theme keys below are per-machine preferences kept OUT of the synced common file — override each as this machine needs. Anything the CLI writes into the rendered file (/model, /config, `claude plugin enable -s user`) is captured back into this file by the next install.sh run, so preferences are not lost.
_shadowing_warning: Claude Code honours exactly ONE settings.local.json — the NEAREST one. Inside a project that has its own .claude/settings.local.json with an enabledPlugins map, that map fully REPLACES this file's map (no per-key merge), so plugins enabled ONLY here are silently disabled in that project — no error, and `install.sh`/plugin_sync still report green (they only warn). Entries in config/settings.json are immune: they always merge in. So for a plugin you want everywhere, either add it to the lab-wide config/settings.json, or re-declare it in each project's own settings.local.json. Always confirm with `claude plugin list` run FROM the project directory, never from $HOME. Verified 2026-07-27.
_optional_plugins_note: Opt-in personal plugins (NOT enabled lab-wide — absent from config/settings.json, marketplaces not in extraKnownMarketplaces): remotion@remotion, ui-ux-pro-max@ui-ux-pro-max-skill, marketing-skills@marketingskills, claude-mem@thedotmack (marketplace name is 'thedotmack', not 'claude-mem'). Enable by running /sync-claudebase (step 4k detects, asks per plugin, then registers the marketplace + installs at user scope), or manually: `claude plugin marketplace add <ref> && claude plugin install <name> -s user`. List each one you enable here (e.g. "remotion@remotion": true) — that is what re-enables it on the next render, and what keeps future syncs from flagging it as reverse drift. But listing it here is NOT enough to make it active inside a project that ships its own enabledPlugins map — see _shadowing_warning. Verify with `claude plugin list` that Status reads 'enabled', not merely installed. claude-mem adds session-start injection and needs the `bun` runtime — see docs/ai-usage-fitting.md before keeping it.
